root_cause: AI sight was driven by the renderer. Only EngineGL33::UpdateFogMedium called SetFogSight, and it passed nullptr whenever this frame's fog did not draw: post effects off, SSAA off, fog unavailable, or a vehicle interior. A dedicated server or headless process never called it at all. The sight map was also built inside the fog stage (UpdateFogFloor) from the terrain horizon map, so it existed only after the fog first drew, and only while terrainShadows or terrainOcclusion was above 0. A probe proved this using the new triFogSight command (Eden, 06:10, overcast 0.7, setFog 0.3). With post effects on, the drawn fog and AI both had mist 1.950e-03. With post effects off, AI went inactive (ai=0, mist 0) even though the weather still held the mist.
change_summary: AI sight is now part of the simulation. World::SimulateLandscape calls the new SimulateFogSight(GLOB_LAND) once per step, after the clock, sun and weather move and before PerformAI. When the island's heights change, it builds the sight map at once on the main thread with BuildFogSightMap. That map uses the same box downsample as the terrain horizon map (DownsampleTerrainGrid) plus the fog floor and the mist layer, and does not depend on any render setting (Eden 1024x1024: about 150 ms). Each step, the medium comes from ComputeFogMedium(WorldFogInputs(land), GEngine tuning or the base defaults, applied=true). The renderer no longer calls SetFogSight. It fills its own medium from the same WorldFogInputs function and draws its fog floor texture from AI sight's map (FogSightMapInUse), so the drawn mist sits where AI finds it from the first frame, even with terrain shadows off. A rate-limited warning fires if the drawn mist or humid air ever differs from AI's. Pure helpers added: FogSightTransmittanceThrough, FogSightMedium, FogSightMapInUse, UpdateFogSightMedium, and Set/GetDrawnFogMedium (probe readout only; AI never reads it). triFogSight reports AI transmittance next to the drawn transmittance and the classic tactical fog. After the fix, with post effects off: ai=1, mist 1.952e-03, the same as with the fog drawn. With fogMist=0.5 and fogDensity=2, the AI values equal the drawn values exactly. The drawn fog is unchanged: dawn_valley after vs the round-3 final has a mean absolute difference of 0.75/255 and a 99th percentile of 7.

Three new cases in test_volumetric_fog.cpp. (1) AI sight equals the drawn fog's air for the same inputs and knobs, across fogDensity 0.5/1/2 times fogMist 0/0.5/1: the AI medium fields equal ComputeFogMedium(in,t,true), FogSightTransmittance equals the march through the renderer's medium, and the knobs move AI the same way. root_cause: (a) The sun disc was drawn in the low sun's own colour (about 1, 0.62, 0.3). The hue-keeping curve only whitens light past white by 1 - kChromaKeep*chroma^2 (0.61), which gives (255,237,220) on paper; the shots measure (255,238,219), so the disc was a peach dot. The sky roll-off had a single cap everywhere (kSkyRolloffCap 2.4, about 0.85 of white), so the aureole round a low sun was pressed into a plateau: the radial profile in lowsun_fp at 960 reads 237,206,164 from 8 to 24 px, then falls. (c) The disc was drawn by its angle from the sun, so the rectilinear projection stretched it near the frame corner. Axis ratio measured 1.23 at 960 and 1.27 at 1080 (1080 was also oval). (d) The shafts come from the volumetric fog's near pass (psFogNear). Moving the pass's soft cap before the lit share, or using the lit share linearly, changed nothing. A 2.5x gain override drew clear shafts, so kFogBeamGain was simply too low. (b) With fogDensity=0 the bay is crisp. fogMist, fogSun, camAerial, turning off the humid ground air and widening the ring's exclusion round the sun all left it unchanged. So the cause is the clear haze's in-scatter on the sun side, lit by the brightest horizon sky (the ring).
change_summary: Sky roll-off (PhotoCamera.hpp/.cpp and GLSL camSkyRolloff(lin, d)): near the sun the cap now rises from 2.4 to kSkySunCap 10 (past white) along 1/(1+2(1-cos)/r^2), with r = 1.2 degrees. Every caller passes its direction (dome, clouds, aerial colour, sky reflection). New C++ mirrors: SkySunGlow, SkyRolloffCapToward, SkyRolloffToward. Sun disc (camSunDisc): it is solved per pixel in screen space from dFdx/dFdy as an equal-area circle, so it is round anywhere in the frame. Its colour goes kSunDiscWhite 0.85 of the way to white from 4 degrees up and keeps its colour at the horizon. kFogBeamGain goes from 14 to 35 so the shafts read. Results: the disc is (255,255,254) and round (axis ratio 1.00 to 1.02 at 960 and 1080). At 960 the glow falls off smoothly: 253 at 8 px, 248 at 16 px, 238 at 32 px, 223 at 48 px, with no plateau. pine_rays shafts read at thumbnail size and the sky round them is unchanged. dawn_valley is not fixed (bay contrast is the same before and after).
remaining: (b) dawn_valley's bay is still veiled by cream haze on the sun side. Likely root fix: the haze's light toward a low sun should follow the phase function at the ray's own angle to the sun. Today the ring samples the sky 2 degrees or more above the land, which brings the aureole's flank into the haze. This needs the ring's sample elevation in the injection. Under a 12x high-pass the glow shows fine one-level rings, as round 3 did, plus one ring where coastline_sunset's peach core glow ends; neither is visible at full size or thumbnail. The halo is smaller than landed's painted sprite: a kSkySunGlowRad of 1.8 to 2 degrees would come closer but adds bright sky. The broad cream low-sun sky (camHaze 6) is unchanged. Night and grey views were not reshot (the cap only rises within a few degrees of the sun and only above the knee). root_cause: (a) The setFog medium was several times denser than the classic fog at mid range. The weather fog was 2.8 times the classic extinction (kSetFogBoost). On top of it sat the grey-deck haze gain, which was cut only for rain, and a valley mist weighted 1.2 x fog. The game log at fog 0.3 under the 0.7 deck: weather 5.7e-3/m with the boost, haze 1.31e-3, mist 1.09e-3. A probe colouring the fog's view depth puts the rock at 200-400 m and the tree line at 300-500 m, where 15% and less of the surface was left; vanilla keeps the first 300 m or more crisp. volFog=0 brings them back; surfaces=0 and photoLight=0 do not. (c) Under a full grey deck the camera dome drew the painted deck at full cloud light, high in the curve's shoulder, which squeezed its relief to a spread of about 10 levels. The fog apply leaves the upper sky alone. (b) Specks: the probes show they do not come from the fog apply, the overlay snapshot, sky-classified MSAA edges, the near field, GTAO, SSR, the canopy, camLocal or bloom. taa=0 with sharpen=0 removes nearly all of them. Clamping the TAA history did not help, so the bad value is already in the composite output of the jittered frame. The exact cause is not found.

root_cause: (a) The guess that the burst light reaches its whole cloud was wrong. Probe 1 (round 3 code, same burst shot paused at fixed ages, with and without combatSmoke=0) gave the same picture at every age. The cloud was exactly its CfgCloudlets Explosion temperature-table colour (white at 2200 K, lemon at 1900 K, mustard at 1600 K). Cause: the fireball puffs use a self-lit (MSShining) shape. Object::DrawDecal draws one as its table colour times the eye's accommodation, which the photoreal camera holds at 1. So the fireball showed one flat table colour, never brighter than a white wall. A first fix applied only in the lit branch changed nothing, which confirmed the puffs take the self-lit branch. (b) Under the camera a burst's light on surfaces reached 20 m. Seen from 2 m at 60 to 90 m that lit disc squashes into a 9 px strip, brighter than the fireball. (c) The dusk ground is metered nearly as dark as night, so the wreck's fire at day scale 0.12 still lit the plain behind it. (d) The composite's hue-keeping curve mixed all three channels toward white by one amount, so bright orange (1, 0.55, 0.16) became cream (1, 0.68, 0.38).
change_summary: (a) New FireballPuff and BlackBodyRgb in CombatLights. A puff counts as a fireball when its table tops out between 1500 and 3000 (read as kelvin). Camp fire smoke and smoke shells (1000), gun fire (4200) and crater smoke are excluded. A fireball puff glows the colour of a black body at its temperature. Brightness follows Wien's law at 580 nm, each channel softly saturated at 2 so the hottest core goes white-yellow. What it reflects is dark soot. Object::DrawDecal sends a fireball puff under the combat lights through the lit branch: scene light on the soot, then the glow added and carried past 1 as decal glow. Cloudlet gained Temperature() and HottestTemperature(). CombatSmokeTransmittance now also applies to Explosion, so a burst lights its cloud's base and near side. Fixed-age probe result: 6 frames yellow-white fireball, 8 frames orange fireball with dark puffs, 10 frames and later dark grey-brown smoke. (b) Under the camera an Explosion's surface light now ends at 3 ball radii (7.8 m for a heavy shell); cannon flashes keep 20 m. Horizon band beside a 1 frame old burst, 99th percentile: 60 -> 32 (ground 28). (c) New CombatTwilight(sun elevation), camera only, scales steady lights (fire, flare, motor) on surfaces and in the air. It is 1 at 6 degrees or more under the horizon (night unchanged), 10 times lower per 2.5 degrees above that, floor 0.1. Flames and smoke keep their full brightness. Wreck horizon 99th percentile 48 -> 31; the line is gone. (d) Each channel now whitens by w^(1 + 3(1 - its share of the peak)), in GLSL and in the C++ mirror (which also gained the chroma keep it lacked). town_night: flame core (239,199,150) -> (239,188,108), stones top tenth (254,225,194) -> (254,206,130), fully white pixels in the fire box 171 -> 0, plume unchanged. town_fog_night: white pixels 597 -> 0.

root_cause: Two causes. (1) The sky table's clear sky has the right chromaticity: the overhaul's zenith ratios (0.34,0.56,1) match landed's (0.36,0.59,1) and the real sky's. But the overhaul draws it at the physical scale (about a third of landed's linear light), and the hue-keeping curve keeps those ratios exactly. A real camera's per-channel film curve deepens a mid-tone blue. So a dim sky with landed's ratios read as slate (91,114,148). Probe 1 ruled out fog (volFog=0 changed it by 2 levels), white balance (camWb=0, 2 levels) and haze (camHaze=1, about 5 levels). Probe 2 used a shader override that raised only the clear sky's chroma, and the sky turned clean blue at the same luminance. (2) Over a bright plain the camera exposed 0.63 EV under the average scene: kBrightKeep -0.45 times the meter's 0.84 EV, plus kCameraHighSunEv -0.25 (readout ev=-0.35). That darkened both the ground (Sinai sand 149 against 186) and the sky. Probe 1 with camEv +0.5 lifted both.
change_summary: 1) Exposure: kBrightKeep -0.45 -> -0.05 (PhotoCamera.hpp). Only scenes brighter than the average scene change. A bright plain at noon is still about 0.3 EV under the average scene through kCameraHighSunEv. noon_fields ev -0.35 -> -0.01, sinai 0.03 -> 0.33, jeep_close_noon +0.2 EV. Golden, evening, town_noon, noon_vista, overcast and night views keep their exposure to within 0.02 EV. 2) New camSkyDeepen in camSkyLook (EngineGL33_LightingShadersSky.cpp), with a C++ mirror DaySkyDeepen and DaySkyDeepWeight (PhotoCamera.cpp/.hpp). It scales the clear sky's chroma about its luminance in linear light by 1 + 0.65*w, keeping luminance and dominant hue, and no channel goes under 0.25 of the luminance. w applies by day only (sun 8..25 deg), above the horizon band (view sine 0.03..0.4) and away from the sun's glow, and is zero under the weather's veil. It feeds the dome, the aerial-perspective colour and the sea's sky reflection; clouds are untouched. Results at 1080p: noon_fields sky top (91,114,148) -> (74,121,173), horizon paler (120,148,180), ground 140 -> 152. Sinai sky top (86,109,144) -> (66,115,168), sand 149 -> 158. jeep_close_noon ground 160 -> 168 (vanilla 169). noon_vista sky top (118,152,201) -> (89,146,212). An A/B at the same sim clock shows forest_edge_golden and woods_pine2_evening unchanged to within 1 level. town_night differs only in the smoke puffs (particle timing). New unit cases are in test_photo_camera.cpp, and the shader-constant pins are in test_remaster_lighting.cpp. clang-format is clean.
